claim: Ubiquitination regulates multiple steps in the membrane protein lifecycle.
source: Ubiquitination determines membrane protein functional expression by regulating multiple steps in the membrane protein lifecycle.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction section of the manuscript.

claim: The human genome encodes 2 E1s, 37 E2s, and >600 E3 ubiquitin ligases.
source: The human genome encodes 2 E1s, 37 E2s, and >600 E3 ubiquitin ligases.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the human genome composition presented in the introduction.

claim: Ubiquitin contains seven lysine residues (K6, K11, K27, K29, K33, K48, K63) that can serve as secondary attachment points to make diverse polyubiquitin chains.
source: Ubiquitin contains seven lysine residues (K6, K11, K27, K29, K33, K48, K63) that, together with its N-terminus (Met1), can serve as secondary attachment points to make diverse polyubiquitin chains with different structures and functions (Komander, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Komander, 2009.

claim: KCNQ1 together with auxiliary KCNE1 subunits give rise to the slowly activating delayed rectifier current IKs that is important for human ventricular action potential repolarization.
source: KCNQ1 (Kv7.1; Q1), is a voltage-gated K+ channel which together with auxiliary KCNE1 subunits give rise to the slowly activating delayed rectifier current IKs that is important for human ventricular action potential repolarization (Barhanin et al., 1996; Sanguinetti et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Barhanin et al., 1996 and Sanguinetti et al., 1996.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in Q1 lead to long QT syndrome type 1 (LQT1).
source: Loss-of-function mutations in Q1 lead to long QT syndrome type 1 (LQT1), a precarious condition that predisposes affected individuals to exertion-triggered cardiac arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death (Tester et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Tester et al., 2005.

claim: NEDD4-2 binds a PY motif on Q1 C-terminus and enhances Q1 ubiquitination.
source: In heterologous expression studies, NEDD4-2, a HECT domain E3 ligase, binds a PY motif on Q1 C-terminus; enhances Q1 ubiquitination; down-regulates Q1 expression; and inhibits IKs current (Jespersen et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jespersen et al., 2007.

claim: NEDD4-2 down-regulates Q1 expression and inhibits IKs current.
source: In heterologous expression studies, NEDD4-2, a HECT domain E3 ligase, binds a PY motif on Q1 C-terminus; enhances Q1 ubiquitination; down-regulates Q1 expression; and inhibits IKs current (Jespersen et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jespersen et al., 2007.

claim: nanoCHIP was generated by replacing the TPR domain of CHIP with the vhh4 nanobody.
source: We substituted the TPR domain of CHIP with the vhh4 nanobody, which binds GFP/YFP (but not CFP) (Kubala et al., 2010), creating nanoCHIP.
evidence: This describes the molecular engineering approach used to create nanoCHIP.

claim: The vhh4 nanobody binds GFP/YFP but not CFP.
source: We substituted the TPR domain of CHIP with the vhh4 nanobody, which binds GFP/YFP (but not CFP) (Kubala et al., 2010), creating nanoCHIP.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kubala et al., 2010.

claim: nanoCHIP dramatically reduced surface density of BBS-Q1-YFP while minimally affecting total protein expression.
source: Test cells expressing nanoCHIP + BBS-Q1-YFP showed little change in YFP fluorescence compared to control (YFP = 577 ± 11 a.f.u, n = 1727 for nano; YFP = 630 ± 18 a.f.u, n = 783 for nanoCHIP), suggesting that the presumed targeted ubiquitination did not substantively affect Q1 stability (Figure 2D,E). By contrast, the surface density of BBS-Q1-YFP between the two conditions revealed an entirely different picture. Whereas control cells (nano) displayed a sizable population of surface BBS-Q1-YFP as reported by robust mean red fluorescence signal (BTX647 = 822 ± 26 a.f.u, n = 4837), this surface pool was almost completely eliminated in cells co-expressing nanoCHIP (BTX647 = 55 ± 2 a.f.u, n = 2257) (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative flow cytometry data presented in the text and referenced figures.

claim: nanoCHIP had no effect on surface expression of BBS-Q1 channels lacking the YFP tag.
source: To assess specificity, we co-expressed nanoCHIP with BBS-Q1. In sharp contrast to the result obtained with BBS-Q1-YFP, nanoCHIP had no effect on surface expression of BBS-Q1 channels (BTX647 = 527 ± 16 a.f.u, n = 6425 for nano; BTX647 = 633 ± 24 a.f.u, n = 3657 for nanoCHIP) (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative flow cytometry data demonstrating specificity of the approach.

claim: A CHIP deletion mutant (nanoCHIP*) that abolishes E3 ligase activity did not alter Q1 surface expression.
source: As a further control, co-expression of a CHIP deletion mutant (nanoCHIP*) that abolishes E3 ligase activity (Nikolay et al., 2004) did not alter Q1 surface expression, confirming the requirement of catalytic activity for nanoCHIP-dependent surface modulation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and a citation to Nikolay et al., 2004.

claim: nanoNSlmb and nanoMDM2 reduced BBS-Q1-YFP surface density with minimal effects on total expression.
source: We obtained qualitatively similar results with nanoNSlmb and nanoMDM2 to what we observed with nanoCHIP in that they all reduced BBS-Q1-YFP surface density with minimal effects on total expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: nanoNEDD4-2 diminished total Q1-YFP expression concomitant with decreased surface expression.
source: Interestingly, nanoNEDD4-2 diminished total Q1-YFP expression concomitant with the decreased surface expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Both effects of nanoNEDD4-2 on Q1 stability and surface density were abolished with co-expression of a NEDD4-2 catalytic inactive mutant (nanoNEDD4-2*).
source: Both effects on Q1 stability and surface density were abolished with co-expression of a NEDD4-2 catalytic inactive mutant (nanoNEDD4-2*) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Q1 is known to be ubiquitinated and regulated by heterologously expressed wild-type NEDD4-2.
source: Q1 is known to be ubiquitinated and regulated by heterologously expressed wild-type NEDD4-2 (Jespersen et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jespersen et al., 2007.

claim: Co-expression with NEDD4-2 reduced the total expression of Q1-YFP.
source: Densitometric analyses of the bands indicated that co-expression with NEDD4-2 reduced the total expression of Q1-YFP (Figure 3A; area under the curve), in agreement with previous results (Jespersen et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by densitometric analysis data in Figure 3A and a citation to Jespersen et al., 2007.

claim: Co-expression of NEDD4-2 substantially increased Q1-YFP ubiquitination compared to control.
source: Co-expression of NEDD4-2 substantially increased Q1-YFP ubiquitination compared to the control condition (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data presented in Figure 3B,C.

claim: nanoCHIP did not substantively affect Q1-YFP total expression.
source: Consistent with the flow cytometry experiments, nanoCHIP did not substantively affect Q1-YFP total expression (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data presented in Figure 3D.

claim: nanoCHIP significantly augmented Q1-YFP ubiquitination compared to control.
source: Nevertheless, nanoCHIP significantly augmented Q1-YFP ubiquitination compared to the control condition, although the effect was smaller than observed with NEDD4-2 (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data presented in Figure 3E,F.

claim: The effect of nanoCHIP on Q1-YFP ubiquitination was smaller than observed with NEDD4-2.
source: Nevertheless, nanoCHIP significantly augmented Q1-YFP ubiquitination compared to the control condition, although the effect was smaller than observed with NEDD4-2 (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data presented in Figure 3E,F.

claim: The interaction of KCNE1 with Q1 transforms the current waveform from small and rapidly activating to large and slowly activating (IKs).
source: The interaction of KCNE1 with Q1 transforms the current waveform from one which is small and rapidly activating (Q1 alone) to one that is large and slowly activating (IKs; Q1 + KCNE1) (Barhanin et al., 1996; Sanguinetti et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Barhanin et al., 1996 and Sanguinetti et al., 1996.

claim: nanoCHIP dramatically reduced surface density of BBS-Q1-YFP co-expressed with KCNE1.
source: Similar to our observations with Q1 alone, nanoCHIP dramatically reduced surface density of BBS-Q1-YFP co-expressed with KCNE1 (Figure 4A–C), while minimally affecting total protein expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data presented in Figure 4A–C.

claim: nanoCHIP had no effect on channel surface density in cells expressing BBS-Q1 + KCNE1 (lacking a YFP tag).
source: This effect was selective, as in cells expressing BBS-Q1 + KCNE1 (lacking a YFP tag), nanoCHIP had no effect on channel surface density (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data presented in Figure 4D–F.

claim: nanoCHIP targeted to KCNE1-YFP effectively and selectively eliminated surface channels.
source: Finally, we wondered whether we could manipulate the surface expression of Q1 by targeting nanoCHIP to the auxiliary KCNE1 subunit. Indeed, in cells expressing BBS-Q1 + KCNE1-YFP, nanoCHIP effectively and selectively eliminated surface channels (Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), demonstrating the potential power of the approach to sculpt ion channel macromolecular complexes by targeting accessory proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data presented in Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: nanoCHIP targeted to KCNE1-YFP markedly increased ubiquitination of co-expressed Q1.
source: Consistent with these results, nanoCHIP targeted to KCNE1-YFP markedly increased ubiquitination of co-expressed Q1 (Figure 4J,K).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data presented in Figure 4J,K.

claim: Control CHO cells transfected with Q1-YFP + KCNE1 + nano displayed robust outward K+ currents with the signature slow activation kinetics of IKs.
source: Control Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells transfected with Q1-YFP + KCNE1 + nano displayed robust outward K+ currents with the signature slow activation kinetics of IKs, which were essentially eliminated by nanoCHIP (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data presented in Figure 5A–C.

claim: IKs currents were essentially eliminated by nanoCHIP in CHO cells.
source: Control Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells transfected with Q1-YFP + KCNE1 + nano displayed robust outward K+ currents with the signature slow activation kinetics of IKs, which were essentially eliminated by nanoCHIP (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data presented in Figure 5A–C.

claim: nanoCHIP had no effect on IKs reconstituted with subunits that lacked the YFP tag.
source: By contrast, nanoCHIP had no effect on IKs reconstituted with subunits that lacked the YFP tag (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data presented in Figure 5D–F.

claim: Switching the YFP tag to KCNE1 yielded IKs that was significantly reduced by nanoCHIP.
source: Finally, switching the YFP tag to KCNE1 also yielded IKs that was significantly reduced by nanoCHIP (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data presented in Figure 5G–I.

claim: The inducible nanoCHIP (iN-CHIP) approach enables acute temporal control of ubiquitination of specific target proteins.
source: We next sought to exploit the rapamycin-induced heterodimerization system to develop an approach that enables acute temporal control of ubiquitination of specific target proteins (Crabtree and Schreiber, 1996).
evidence: This describes the development of the iN-CHIP system with a citation to Crabtree and Schreiber, 1996.

claim: A measurable effect of rapamycin on surface BBS-Q1-YFP was seen within 20 min of rapamycin addition.
source: A measurable effect was seen within 20 min of rapamycin addition to the transfected HEK293 cells; the half-life for reduction of surface channels was 209 ± 17 mins (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry time-course data presented in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The half-life for reduction of surface channels by iN-CHIP was 209 ± 17 mins.
source: A measurable effect was seen within 20 min of rapamycin addition to the transfected HEK293 cells; the half-life for reduction of surface channels was 209 ± 17 mins (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry time-course data and exponential decay fitting presented in Figure 6B,C.

claim: Rapamycin treatment for 20 hr had no impact on Q1 surface density in cells expressing BBS-Q1 together with FRB-CHIP and FKBP-nano.
source: In control experiments, rapamycin treatment for 20 hr had no impact on Q1 surface density in cells expressing BBS-Q1 together with FRB-CHIP and FKBP-nano (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by control data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: When cells were pretreated with rapamycin for 3 hr, delivery of new BBS-Q1-YFP channels to the surface plateaued at a value ~75% lower compared to control.
source: When this experiment was conducted in the absence of rapamycin pre-treatment, we observed robust delivery of new BBS-Q1-YFP to the cell surface during the chase period with a half-life of ~36 ± 3 mins (Figure 7B). When cells were pretreated with rapamycin for 3 hr, delivery of new channels to the surface plateaued at a value ~75% lower compared to control (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by optical pulse-chase assay data presented in Figure 7B.

claim: iN-CHIP-induced ubiquitination of BBS-Q1-YFP compromises forward trafficking of channels to the cell surface.
source: Thus, iN-CHIP-induced ubiquitination of BBS-Q1-YFP compromises forward trafficking of channels to the cell surface.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the forward trafficking assay data.

claim: Pre-activation of iN-CHIP with a 3 hr rapamycin pre-treatment had no impact on the rate of BBS-Q1-YFP internalization.
source: Surprisingly, pre-activation of iN-CHIP with a 3 hr rapamycin pre-treatment had no impact on the rate of BBS-Q1-YFP internalization (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by internalization assay data presented in Figure 7D.

claim: nanoCHIP reduces BBS-Q1-YFP surface density by selectively reducing forward trafficking of the channel.
source: Together, the results indicate that nanoCHIP reduces BBS-Q1-YFP surface density by selectively reducing forward trafficking of the channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined forward trafficking and internalization assay data.

claim: Control cardiomyocytes expressing BBS-Q1-YFP + nano displayed strong YFP/CFP fluorescence as well as QD655 signal on the sarcolemma.
source: Control cells expressing BBS-Q1-YFP + nano displayed strong YFP/CFP fluorescence as well as QD655 signal on the sarcolemma, indicating robust cell surface density of the channel (Figure 8A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data presented in Figure 8A,C.

claim: Cardiomyocytes co-expressing nanoCHIP showed a sharply depressed QD655 signal.
source: By contrast, cardiomyocytes co-expressing nanoCHIP showed a sharply depressed QD655 signal (Figure 8B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data presented in Figure 8B,C.

claim: YFP fluorescence was not significantly different between cardiomyocytes expressing nano versus nanoCHIP.
source: YFP fluorescence was not significantly different between the two experimental conditions (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data presented in Figure 8D.

claim: nanoCHIP is effective in cardiomyocytes and selectively down-regulates BBS-Q1-YFP surface pool.
source: These data demonstrate that nanoCHIP is effective in cardiomyocytes, and selectively down-regulates BBS-Q1-YFP surface pool in this native cellular context.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cardiomyocyte experiments.

claim: nanoCHIP selectively eliminated the surface CaV1.2 pool with no impact on total BBS-α1C-YFP expression.
source: Similar to our observations with Q1, nanoCHIP selectively eliminated the surface CaV1.2 pool with no impact on total BBS-α1C-YFP expression (Figure 9B–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data presented in Figure 9B–E.

claim: nanoCHIP essentially abolished CaV1.2 currents reconstituted in HEK 293 cells.
source: Consistent with these results, nanoCHIP essentially abolished CaV1.2 currents reconstituted in HEK 293 cells (Figure 9F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data presented in Figure 9F,G.

claim: Targeted ubiquitination of Q1 and CaV1.2 with nanoCHIP yielded impaired trafficking and functional inactivation without frank degradation of the protein.
source: In comparison, our results suggest a fundamental difference between ion channels and cytosolic proteins in which targeted ubiquitination with nanoCHIP (as well as nanoNSlmb and nanoMDM2) yielded impaired trafficking and functional inactivation without frank degradation of the protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined data on Q1 and CaV1.2.

claim: Absolute degradation is not necessary for potent functional knockdown of Q1 and CaV1.2 channels.
source: As such, our results indicate that absolute degradation is not necessary for potent functional knockdown of Q1 and CaV1.2 channels, and highlight the importance of employing functional/cell biological assays to assess the efficacy of post-translational knockdown.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: nanoNEDD4-2 can selectively degrade the ion channel Q1 in situ.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrate here that nanoNEDD4-2 can selectively degrade the ion channel Q1 in situ, emphasizing the potential for customized protein manipulation with engineered E3 ligases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the nanoNEDD4-2 experiments.

claim: Modest changes in total ubiquitination intensity as detected by conventional Western blot can result in substantial functional and cell biological effects on ion channel surface trafficking.
source: As such, our findings suggest that modest changes in total ubiquitination intensity as detected by conventional Western blot can result in substantial functional and cell biological effects on ion channel surface trafficking.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ubiquitination and trafficking data.

claim: CHIP is a U-box E3 ligase comprised of a catalytic domain that binds E2 and a tetratricopeptide repeats (TPR) targeting domain that binds Hsp70.
source: For example, CHIP (C-terminus of the Hsp70-interacting protein), is a U-box E3 ligase comprised of a catalytic domain that binds E2 and a tetratricopeptide repeats (TPR) targeting domain that binds Hsp70 (Connell et al., 2001; Murata et al., 2003; Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Connell et al., 2001; Murata et al., 2003; Zhang et al., 2005.

claim: Dysregulation of trafficking, sorting, and degradation processes underlies diverse ion channelopathies including cardiac arrhythmias and cystic fibrosis.
source: Dysregulation of these processes underlies diverse ion channelopathies including cardiac arrhythmias and cystic fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract.

claim: Engineered CHIP enhanced KCNQ1 ubiquitination.
source: Engineered CHIP enhanced KCNQ1 ubiquitination, eliminated KCNQ1 surface-density, and abolished reconstituted K+ currents without affecting protein expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in the results section.

claim: Engineered CHIP eliminated KCNQ1 surface-density.
source: Engineered CHIP enhanced KCNQ1 ubiquitination, eliminated KCNQ1 surface-density, and abolished reconstituted K+ currents without affecting protein expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in the results section.

claim: Engineered CHIP abolished reconstituted K+ currents without affecting protein expression.
source: Engineered CHIP enhanced KCNQ1 ubiquitination, eliminated KCNQ1 surface-density, and abolished reconstituted K+ currents without affecting protein expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in the results section.

claim: KCNQ1 surface-density declined with a ~ 3.5 hr t1/2 by impaired forward trafficking.
source: A chemo-genetic variation enabling chemical control of ubiquitination revealed KCNQ1 surface-density declined with a ~ 3.5 hr t1/2 by impaired forward trafficking.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in the results section (209 ± 17 mins ≈ 3.5 hrs).

claim: Impaired surface trafficking of membrane proteins underlies diverse diseases ranging from cystic fibrosis to cardiac arrhythmias.
source: Impaired surface trafficking of membrane proteins underlies diverse diseases ranging from cystic fibrosis to cardiac arrhythmias (Gelman and Kopito, 2002; Anderson et al., 2014), motivating a need to better understand fundamental mechanisms controlling membrane protein surface density.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Gelman and Kopito, 2002 and Anderson et al., 2014.

claim: The surface repertoire of membrane proteins is regulated by multi-layered maturation and trafficking processes.
source: The surface repertoire of membrane proteins is regulated by multi-layered maturation and trafficking processes (MacGurn et al., 2012; Foot et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to MacGurn et al., 2012 and Foot et al., 2017.

claim: Ubiquitination has classically been ascribed to targeting cytosolic proteins for degradation by the proteasome.
source: Ubiquitination has classically been ascribed to targeting cytosolic proteins for degradation by the proteasome (Hershko and Ciechanover, 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hershko and Ciechanover, 1998.

claim: Ubiquitination of both cytosolic and membrane proteins can lead to more nuanced outcomes including regulating protein trafficking/sorting, stability, and/or function.
source: However, it is now evident that ubiquitination of both cytosolic and membrane proteins can lead to more nuanced outcomes including regulating protein trafficking/sorting, stability, and/or function (Komander, 2009; Foot et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Komander, 2009 and Foot et al., 2017.

claim: Multiple E3 ligases may ubiquitinate a single substrate.
source: Factors that complicate analyses include: (1) multiple E3 ligases may ubiquitinate a single substrate; (2) a particular E3 can typically catalyze ubiquitination of multiple substrates; (3) distinct E3 ligases can have preference for particular ubiquitination profiles (e.g. monoubiquitination versus polyubiquitination) and polyubiquitin chain linkages (e.g. K48 versus K63); (4) lack of temporal control over the ubiquitination process.
evidence: This is stated as a complicating factor in understanding ubiquitination.

claim: A particular E3 can typically catalyze ubiquitination of multiple substrates.
source: Factors that complicate analyses include: (1) multiple E3 ligases may ubiquitinate a single substrate; (2) a particular E3 can typically catalyze ubiquitination of multiple substrates; (3) distinct E3 ligases can have preference for particular ubiquitination profiles (e.g. monoubiquitination versus polyubiquitination) and polyubiquitin chain linkages (e.g. K48 versus K63); (4) lack of temporal control over the ubiquitination process.
evidence: This is stated as a complicating factor in understanding ubiquitination.

claim: Distinct E3 ligases can have preference for particular ubiquitination profiles and polyubiquitin chain linkages.
source: Factors that complicate analyses include: (1) multiple E3 ligases may ubiquitinate a single substrate; (2) a particular E3 can typically catalyze ubiquitination of multiple substrates; (3) distinct E3 ligases can have preference for particular ubiquitination profiles (e.g. monoubiquitination versus polyubiquitination) and polyubiquitin chain linkages (e.g. K48 versus K63); (4) lack of temporal control over the ubiquitination process.
evidence: This is stated as a complicating factor in understanding ubiquitination.

claim: The slowly activating kinetics of IKs is crucial to its physiological role in human cardiac action potential repolarization.
source: The slowly activating kinetics of IKs is crucial to its physiological role in human cardiac action potential repolarization.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: A common assumption is that ubiquitination of membrane proteins enhances their internalization from the cell surface.
source: A common assumption is that ubiquitination of membrane proteins enhances their internalization from the cell surface, although recent results suggest a more complex picture in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section.

claim: Mutation of ubiquitination sites on EGFRs did not abolish their endocytosis.
source: For example, the E3 ligase Cbl is important to the internalization of activated epidermal growth factor receptors (EGFRs). Nevertheless, mutation of ubiquitination sites on EGFRs did not abolish their endocytosis (Huang et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2007.

claim: A ubiquitin-deficient β2 adrenergic receptor was internalized to a similar extent as the wild type protein.
source: Similarly, a ubiquitin-deficient β2 adrenergic receptor was also internalized to a similar extent as the wild type protein (Shenoy et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Shenoy et al., 2001.

claim: Q1 displays a basal level of ubiquitination due to the activity of an endogenous E3 ligase of unknown identity.
source: A complication in our experimental system is that Q1 displays a basal level of ubiquitination due to the activity of an endogenous E3 ligase of unknown identity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section.

claim: The ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway is a prominent quality control mechanism accomplished by chaperone-mediated ubiquitination of misfolded membrane proteins.
source: For example, the ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway is a prominent quality control mechanism which is accomplished by a chaperone-mediated ubiquitination of misfolded membrane proteins which are then retrotranslocated to the cytosol and targeted to the proteasome for degradation (MacGurn et al., 2012; Foot et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to MacGurn et al., 2012 and Foot et al., 2017.

claim: There are ubiquitin-dependent quality control mechanisms present at the Golgi which result in the diversion of membrane proteins to endosomes.
source: There are also ubiquitin-dependent quality control mechanisms present at the Golgi which results in the diversion of membrane proteins to endosomes where they are sorted by the ESCRT system into multi-vesicular bodies and fusion with lysosomes (Fire et al., 1998; MacGurn et al., 2012; Foot et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fire et al., 1998; MacGurn et al., 2012; Foot et al., 2017.

claim: The temporal control and resolution of mRNA interference methods is relatively poor because they are dependent on the degradation of the targeted native protein.
source: The temporal control and resolution of mRNA interference methods is relatively poor because they are dependent on the degradation of the targeted native protein.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section.

claim: Several groups have utilized engineered ubiquitin ligases to target diverse cytosolic proteins for degradation in situ.
source: Indeed, several groups have utilized this approach to target diverse cytosolic proteins for degradation in situ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section.

claim: The first implementation of targeted ubiquitination exploited SKP1-CUL1-F-box (SCF) E3 ligase complexes to target the retinoblastoma tumor suppressor protein for degradation.
source: The first implementation of targeted ubiquitination exploited SKP1-CUL1-F-box (SCF) E3 ligase complexes, in which a peptide motif was fused to a modular F-box-domain-containing protein in order to target the retinoblastoma tumor suppressor protein for degradation by a Cullin/RING E3 ligase complex (Zhou et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2000.

claim: Caussinius et al fused the N-terminus F-box domain of Slmb to vhhGFP4 (NSlmb-vhhGFP4, also termed deGradFP), which effectively degraded various GFP-tagged proteins in Drosophila.
source: Seeking a more generalizable approach, Caussinius et al fused the N-terminus F-box domain of Slmb (a Drosophila melanogaster F-box protein) to vhhGFP4 (NSlmb-vhhGFP4, also termed deGradFP), which effectively degraded various GFP-tagged proteins in Drosophila (Caussinus et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Caussinus et al., 2011.

claim: Approaches that exploit SCF complexes have the potential to sequester endogenous components by over-expressed engineered F-box proteins.
source: Yet because approaches that exploit SCF complexes have the potential to sequester endogenous components by over-expressed engineered F-box proteins (Hatakeyama et al., 2005; Portnoff et al., 2014), other studies have utilized E3 ligases that are not similarly reliant on endogenous scaffold proteins for their mechanism of action.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hatakeyama et al., 2005 and Portnoff et al., 2014.

claim: One approach replaced the substrate binding (TPR) domain of CHIP to enable targeted ubiquitination and degradation of the proto-oncogenes c-Myc and K-Ras.
source: One such approach replaced the substrate binding (TPR) domain of CHIP to enable targeted ubiquitination and degradation of the proto-oncogenes c-Myc (Hatakeyama et al., 2005) and K-Ras (Ma et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hatakeyama et al., 2005 and Ma et al., 2013.

claim: Replacing the TPR of CHIP with intrabodies directed against β-galactosidase and maltose binding protein yielded effective destruction of these target proteins in transfected HEK293 cells.
source: Further proof of concept experiments replaced the TPR of CHIP with intrabodies directed against β-galactosidase and maltose binding protein, which yielded effective destruction of these target proteins in transfected HEK293 cells (Portnoff et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Portnoff et al., 2014.

claim: A technique referred to as Trim-Away exploits the high affinity of the E3 ligase TRIM21 for the Fc domain of antibodies for selective degradation of target proteins.
source: More recently, a technique referred to as Trim-Away exploits the high affinity of the E3 ligase TRIM21 for the Fc domain of antibodies for selective degradation of target proteins (Clift et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clift et al., 2017.

claim: All previous renditions of engineered E3 ligase technology have relied on degradation of target proteins as the ultimate expression of efficacy.
source: Without exception, all previous renditions of this technology have relied on degradation of target proteins as the ultimate expression of efficacy.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section.

claim: Many ion channels are multi-protein complexes made up minimally of pore-forming proteins associated with accessory subunits.
source: Many ion channels, including Q1, are multi-protein complexes made up minimally of pore-forming proteins associated with accessory subunits.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section.

claim: Q1 can associate with any of five KCNE auxiliary subunits (KCNE1-KCNE5), each of which confers distinctive functional properties.
source: For example, Q1 can associate with any of five KCNE auxiliary subunits (KCNE1-KCNE5), each of which confers distinctive functional properties (Sun et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sun et al., 2012.

claim: Some KCNE subunits may interact with other K+ channel pore-forming subunits.
source: Moreover, some KCNE subunits may interact with other K+ channel pore-forming subunits (Abbott et al., 1999; Abbott, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Abbott et al., 1999 and Abbott, 2016.

claim: Cardiac ventricular myocytes express all five KCNE subunits together with Q1.
source: Cardiac ventricular myocytes express all five KCNE subunits together with Q1 (Radicke et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Radicke et al., 2006.

claim: Gain-of-function mutations in distinct ion channels cause diverse diseases including inherited erythromelalgia, paroxysmal extreme pain disorder, familial hemiplegic migraine, Timothy syndrome, heritable skeletal dysplasia, short QT syndrome, and familial atrial fibrillation.
source: Gain-of-function mutations in distinct ion channels cause diverse diseases including but not limited to: (NaV1.7) inherited erythromelalgia and paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (Waxman, 2013); (CaV2.1) familial hemiplegic migraine (Pietrobon, 2010); (CaV1.2) Timothy syndrome (Splawski et al., 2004); (TrpV4) heritable skeletal dysplasia (Rock et al., 2008); (KCNQ1 and HERG) short QT syndrome and familial atrial fibrillation (Giudicessi and Ackerman, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to Waxman, 2013; Pietrobon, 2010; Splawski et al., 2004; Rock et al., 2008; Giudicessi and Ackerman, 2012.

claim: Various methods to develop antibody mimetic proteins have recently emerged, including nanobodies, single chain variable fragments (scFv), DARPins, and FingRs/monobodies.
source: Various methods to develop such antibody mimetic proteins have recently emerged, including; nanobodies, single chain variable fragments (scFv), DARPins, and FingRs/monobodies (Koide et al., 1998; Pardon et al., 2014; Plückthun, 2015; Gross et al., 2016; Sha et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Koide et al., 1998; Pardon et al., 2014; Plückthun, 2015; Gross et al., 2016; Sha et al., 2017.

claim: A chemical strategy has been developed that utilizes hetero-bivalent small molecules referred to as PROTACS (proteolysis-targeting chimeras) to bridge endogenous substrates to endogenous ubiquitin ligases.
source: Furthermore, a chemical strategy has been developed that utilizes hetero-bivalent small molecules referred to as PROTACS (proteolysis-targeting chimeras) to bridge endogenous substrates to endogenous ubiquitin ligases (Schneekloth et al., 2004; Lai and Crews, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Schneekloth et al., 2004 and Lai and Crews, 2017.

claim: CaV1.2 mediates excitation-contraction coupling and excitation-transcription coupling in heart and neurons, respectively.
source: Cav1.2 mediates excitation-contraction coupling and excitation-transcription coupling in heart and neurons, respectively, and is comprised of a pore-forming α1C and accessory (β, α2δ, γ) subunits (Catterall, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Catterall, 2000.

claim: The nanoCHIP construct featured the coding sequence for GFP nanobody (vhhGFP4) in frame with the minimal catalytic unit of CHIP E3 ligase (residues 128–303), separated by a flexible GSG linker.
source: The nanoCHIP construct was created by gene synthesis (Genewiz), and featured the coding sequence for GFP nanobody (vhhGFP4) (Kubala et al., 2010) in frame with the minimal catalytic unit of CHIP E3 ligase (residues 128–303), separated by a flexible GSG linker.
evidence: This describes the molecular construction of nanoCHIP.

claim: The catalytically inactive nanoCHIP* was created by deleting the coiled-coil domain [Δ128–229].
source: To create the catalytically inactive nanoCHIP*, we deleted the coiled-coil domain [Δ128–229] as previously described (Nikolay et al., 2004), by amplifying the U-box domain of CHIP E3 ligase (residues 230–303), and cloned this fragment into nano-xx-P2A-CFP using AscI/AflII sites separated by a flexible GSG linker.
evidence: This describes the molecular construction of nanoCHIP* with a citation to Nikolay et al., 2004.

claim: A 13-residue high-affinity bungarotoxin binding site (BBS) was introduced into the extracellular S1-S2 loop of Q1.
source: We introduced a 13-residue high-affinity bungarotoxin binding site (BBS) into the extracellular S1-S2 loop of Q1, enabling detection of surface channels in non-permeabilized cells with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated bungarotoxin (BTX647) (Figure 1C and Figure 2) (Aromolaran et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the molecular engineering approach with a citation to Aromolaran et al., 2014.

claim: The C-terminal YFP tag provides a fluorescent measure of total Q1 expression.
source: The C-terminal YFP tag provides a fluorescent measure of total Q1 expression (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The nanoCHIP construct was generated in a P2A vector that expressed CFP as a separate reporter protein in a 1:1 ratio with nanoCHIP.
source: The nanoCHIP construct was generated in a P2A vector that expressed CFP as a separate reporter protein in a 1:1 ratio with nanoCHIP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.
